core_obligations: Set up the diagram of categories (proof lines 10364-10374): consider the diagonal functor u : C -> C x C together with the two projections, giving morphisms of ringed topoi g, g_1, g_2.

Compute the homotopy of the morphism sets (proof lines 10375-10383): for an object (U_1, U_2) the set of morphisms from the diagonal cosimplicial object is the product of the two morphism sets, which is homotopy equivalent to a point by the simplicial lemma; the auxiliary computation lemma therefore gives L pi_!(g^{-1}K) = L(pi x pi)_!(K).

Conclude (proof lines 10384-10390): applying this to K = g_1^{-1}K_1 tensor^L g_2^{-1}K_2 and using that the pullback commutes with the derived tensor product so that g^{-1}K = K_1 tensor^L K_2, the product-categories lemma finishes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the diagonal and the two projections of the product category.
Show the relevant morphism sets are homotopy equivalent to a point and apply the auxiliary computation lemma.
Specialise to the tensor product of the two pulled-back complexes and apply the product-categories lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Eilenberg-Zilber statement for the functor L pi_!: it commutes with the derived tensor product (statement lines 10350-10361). The proof (proof lines 10363-10390) uses the diagonal and the two projections of the product category, shows the relevant morphism sets are homotopy equivalent to a point, applies the auxiliary computation lemma to the diagonal, and specialises to the tensor product of the pulled-back complexes using the commutation of the pullback with the derived tensor product. H2: one homotopy computation plus one specialisation, written out.
